subtopic: Food Chains, Food Webs and Energy Flow
stem:
The given diagram shows a food chain. Which of the following represents a pyramid of biomass based on the given food chain?

(The food chain is: Aquatic plants → Crustaceans → Small fish → Large fish. Each option is a stacked pyramid diagram. Option a) is an upright four-tier pyramid — widest bar at the bottom narrowing smoothly to the smallest bar at the top. Option b) is an inverted pyramid — widest bar at the top narrowing to the bottom. Option c) is an irregular three-tier figure with a wide base, a wide middle and a small top bar. Option d) is an irregular figure with a wide base, a wider middle bar than the top and a small stub below the base.)

options.label: A
options.text: An upright pyramid — widest at the base (aquatic plants), narrowing to the top (large fish)

options.label: B
options.text: An inverted pyramid — widest at the top, narrowing to the base

options.label: C
options.text: An irregular three-tier figure with a wide base, wide middle and small top

options.label: D
options.text: An irregular figure with a wide base, a wider middle than top and a stub below

stem:
The pH level of precipitation at two places X and Y was found to be as shown in the graph. Which of the following can you deduce from it?

(The figure is a bar chart with pH on the vertical axis from 0 to 10. The bar for place X reaches pH 8 and the bar for place Y reaches pH 4 — rainwater at Y is far more acidic than at X.)

options.label: A
options.text: Marble statues at place X can be seen getting yellowing.

options.label: B
options.text: At place Y, renewable energy sources are fastly replacing use of conventional energy sources.

options.label: C
options.text: Plants at place Y can be seen to have burnt yellow looking leaves.

options.label: D
options.text: At place X there is higher consumption of fossil fuels.

subtopic: Food Chains, Food Webs and Energy Flow
stem:
What does the given flow chart represent?

(The flow chart is a single linear food chain showing energy at each trophic level: Grass 20 units → Deer 2 units → Lion 0.2 units. The energy falls to about one-tenth at each successive level and flows in one direction only.)

options.label: A
options.text: Biomagnification

options.label: B
options.text: Lindeman's law

options.label: C
options.text: Both Unidirectional energy flow and Lindeman's law

options.label: D
options.text: Unidirectional energy flow only

stem:

(The figure is an inverted ecological pyramid — the widest bar is at the top and each successive bar below is narrower, tapering to the thinnest bar at the base.)

options.label: B

subtopic: Food Chains, Food Webs and Energy Flow
stem:
Study the given food web. Which of the following would lead to decrease in the water snail population?

(The food web shows: Hydrilla → Young tadpoles and Hydrilla → Water snails; Young tadpoles → Fish and Water snails → Fish; Water snails → Dragonfly nymphs; Fish → Kingfishers. So Hydrilla is the producer, water snails are eaten by both Fish and Dragonfly nymphs.)

1. Increase in Hydrilla population
2. Increase in young tadpole population
3. Decrease in kingfisher population
4. Increase in dragonfly nymphs population

options.label: A
options.text: (ii), (iii) and (iv) only

options.label: B
options.text: (ii) only

options.label: C
options.text: (i) and (iii) only

options.label: D
options.text: (iv) only

subtopic: Food Chains, Food Webs and Energy Flow
stem:
The table below lists some information about the trophic levels of a food chain.

| Trophic level | Number of organisms | Energy in the trophic level (arbitrary units) |
|---|---|---|
| P | 100 | 10,000 |
| Q | 1 | 100 |
| R | 1000 | 100,000 |
| S | 10 | 1000 |

Which of the following food chains is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: P → Q → R → S

options.label: B
options.text: R → P → Q → S

options.label: C
options.text: P → S → Q → R

options.label: D
options.text: R → P → S → Q

stem:
Refer to the given pie chart regarding contribution of different greenhouse gases and select the incorrect statement regarding it.

(The pie chart shows the share of four greenhouse gases labelled P, Q, R and S: P = 60%, Q = 20%, R = 14% and S = 6%.)

options.label: A
options.text: S is used in aerosol cans, jet fuel, air conditioners and refrigerators.

options.label: B
options.text: Q is also produced by incomplete decomposition mostly by anaerobic methanogens.

options.label: C
options.text: R are synthetic gaseous compounds of carbon and halogen.

options.label: D
options.text: Excessive use of fossil fuel is adding more P to atmosphere.

subtopic: Food Chains, Food Webs and Energy Flow
stem:
The given figure shows a food web in a forest area. In the forest, large amount of insecticides are blown with wind from a nearby field. What will be the effect on the given food web?

(The food web shows: Trees → Flies and Trees → Caterpillars; Flies → Frogs and Flies → Sparrows; Caterpillars → Sparrows; Frogs → Snakes; Sparrows → Snakes and Sparrows → Hawks. Insecticides kill the insects — the flies and caterpillars, which are the primary consumers.)

options.label: A
options.text: Greater reduction in the number of caterpillars than in the number of flies

options.label: B
options.text: Reduction in the number of hawks and snakes

options.label: C
options.text: Increase in the number of frogs

options.label: D
options.text: Increase in the number of sparrows
